title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page finishes the argument of the previous page and then begins a Witt-vector generalization.

(1) Pointwise lemma, needed for part b) of the previous page's Proposition. Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p. Let M be a finite-dimensional k-vector space with a Frobenius-semilinear bijection F_M : M^{(p)} = M ⊗_{k,Frob} k → M. Put E = {x ∈ M : F(x^{(p)}) = x}. Then E is an F_p-space and E ⊗_{F_p} k → M is an isomorphism.
- Proof idea, not written: the map x ↦ F(x^{(p)}) − x is an étale surjective endomorphism of the vector group M (Lang).
- Its kernel is therefore a finite étale group of order p^{dim M}.
- Fixed vectors that are F_p-independent are k-independent (Dieudonné/Lang lemma).

This completes the previous page's Proposition. Over a scheme S of characteristic p, φ : E ↦ (E ⊗_{F_p} O_S, F_E ⊗ 1) is an equivalence between:
- finite étale group schemes killed by p (equivalently, locally constant sheaves of finite-dimensional F_p-vector spaces), and
- locally free O_S-modules with a Frobenius isomorphism F : M^{(p)} ≅ M (unit-root F-modules).

The quasi-inverse is M ↦ ker(F − 1) on the vector group V(M). Rank and isomorphism checks reduce, fibre by fibre, to the lemma.

(2) Generalization from p-torsion to p-power torsion.
- C: finite étale p-group schemes over S that are commutative (implicitly), i.e. locally constant étale sheaves of finite abelian p-groups.
- C': sheaves of modules over the Witt-vector sheaf W_S that are locally isomorphic to finite sums of copies of W_{n,S}, with a Frobenius isomorphism F_M : M^{(p)} ≅ M. The margin says the topology does not matter: 'Zariski or fppf, it's all the same', i.e. descent for W_n-modules.
- C'': schemes in W_S-modules that are smooth (W_n is an affine space, hence smooth).
- Functors: φ(E) = E ⊗_{Z_p} W_S with the obvious F. A functor i : C' → C'' sends M to the scheme representing the sheaf, marked as an isomorphism/equivalence. Finally ψ(E) = E ⊗_{Z_p} W_S as a scheme.

The intended theorem is: finite étale Z/p^n-local systems are equivalent to unit-root F-modules over W_n(O_S). The quasi-inverse takes the kernel of F − 1 on the smooth W_n-module scheme (Lang isogeny / Artin–Schreier–Witt). Passing to the limit gives Z_p-local systems ↔ unit-root F-crystals. This sits within the 1966 crystals correspondence with Tate.
errors: The lemma tacitly needs M finite-dimensional. This is implicit from context (locally free of finite type).
C' should consist of locally free W_n(O_S)-modules of finite type, allowing finite sums of W_{n_i,S} with varying n_i. 'Sum of copies of W_{n,S}' is loose.

C'' as written ('smooth schemes in W_S-modules') carries no Frobenius structure. So i cannot be an equivalence C' ≅ C'' as the '~' suggests. C'' must include the F-isomorphism, or i is only fully faithful onto an image. The page is unfinished here.
Commutativity of the p-groups in C is needed for the tensor product E ⊗_{Z_p} W_S but is not stated.

ideas.what: Over an algebraically closed field, a semilinear Frobenius bijection on a finite-dimensional space is spanned by its fixed points.
ideas.modern_name: Lang–Steinberg / Dieudonné lemma on F-spaces (unit-root F-modules over k̄ are trivial)
ideas.where_published: Standard; e.g. Katz SGA 7 Exp. XXII, Prop. 1.1

ideas.what: Equivalence between étale F_p-local systems on a characteristic-p scheme and locally free O_S-modules with Frobenius isomorphism, via M ↦ ker(F − 1).
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Katz, SGA 7 II Exp. XXII (1973) and 'p-adic properties of modular schemes' (1973)
ideas.where_published: Katz, SGA 7 XXII Prop. 1.1; Katz, Antwerp III §4.1

ideas.what: Witt-vector version: finite étale p-group local systems ↔ W_n(O_S)-modules with Frobenius isomorphism, realized inside smooth W-module schemes as the kernel of F − 1.
ideas.modern_name: Katz correspondence for Z/p^n and Z_p (unit-root F-crystals); Artin–Schreier–Witt theory

ideas.what: Remark that Zariski and fppf topologies give the same category of locally free W_n-modules.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches the Katz correspondence in these notes, attached to the May 1966 Tate letter on crystals. This includes the F_p case with full proof structure on the previous page and the Witt-vector/Z/p^n version here. That would predate Katz's 1973 published treatment, where the result is usually attributed. The dating is uncertain: the folder spans 1966 to after 1970.
missed.quote: C' catégorie des faisceaux en W_S-modules M loc. isomorphes à une somme de copies de W_{n,S}, munis de F_M : M^{(p)} ≅ M ... φ(E) = E ⊗_{Z_p} W_S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical attribution point for the unit-root F-crystal ↔ p-adic local system correspondence, which underlies Katz's work and later Crew and Emerton–Kisin. The mathematics itself is well known.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the well-known Katz correspondence and Lang's lemma. The only interest is the possible priority/dating, since Grothendieck had it sketched (Witt version included) in the crystals papers, possibly as early as 1966. The page is fragmentary and the dating uncertain.
transcription_corrections: The superscript read as 'W_S^{par}' is probably 'W_S^{zar}' (the Zariski sheaf of Witt vectors). This fits the margin note 'Zar ou fppf, c'est kif kif'.
The first line is likely 'Dans un corps de base alg. clos, et à fortiori ... disons :' or similar. The 'p premier' reading is doubtful.
In C the struck words are 'finis loc. libres', replaced by 'finis étales'. The insertion reads 'i.e. des faisceaux en p-groupes loc. constants pour la top. étale'.
'i(M) = schéma qui représente le faisceau...' is correct. The struck text was 'faisceau représentable'.
